reproduction_target: Computational analysis of the Korea10K population-genomic resource: fastp trimming and BWA-MEM alignment of 10,239 30x WGS samples to GRCh38, Picard duplicate marking, GATK BQSR / HaplotypeCaller / GenomicsDBImport joint genotyping / VQSR, multi-step sample and variant QC in PLINK2 (incl. KING relatedness), VEP annotation, permutation-based variant-discovery saturation analysis, SHAPEIT5 phasing plus Minimac3 imputation-panel construction and R-squared benchmarking, 1KGP merge / LD-pruning / PCA / ADMIXTURE population-structure analysis, Y-chromosome liftover + yhaplo haplogrouping + VCF2Dis/IQ-TREE3 phylogeny, mitochondrial NOVOPlasty assembly + bcftools consensus + MitoZ annotation + Haplogrep3 haplogrouping + rotate/MAFFT/IQ-TREE3/MEGA12 phylogeny and divergence dating, xHLA HLA typing, and CG-context-associated-variant (CGV) identification, cross-population allele-frequency comparison and Annotatr/ShinyGO/GeDiPNet functional enrichment. Wet-lab work (blood/saliva collection, DNA extraction, library preparation, MGI DNBSEQ-T7 / Illumina NovaSeq 6000 / HiSeq X Ten sequencing) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis extracted from the Methods sections 'Sample Collection', 'Whole-Genome Sequencing', 'Read Processing and Alignment', 'Variant Calling and Joint Genotyping', 'Sample and Variant Filtering', 'Variant Discovery Saturation Analysis', 'Population Reference Panel Construction and Benchmarking Imputation Performance', 'Population Structure and Admixture Analyses with EBI's 1KGP Reference', 'Y-chromosome phylogenetic reconstruction and haplogroup classification', 'Mitochondrial DNA assembly and quality control', 'Mitochondrial haplogroup classification and phylogenetic reconstruction', 'HLA Typing from Whole-Genome Sequencing Data', 'Identification and Regional Aggregation of CG Context-Associated Variants (CGVs)...', 'Comparing Allele Frequencies of CGVs Across Populations', and 'Genomic Annotation and Functional Enrichment of Hotspot CGVs'. The repository https://github.com/korean-genomics-center/Korea10K landing page and README were read as prose only. The README is 165 bytes and contains only the project title plus an 'In submission' note - no install instructions, no system requirements, no version table, no usage. Top-level directories are admixture_and_pca, backup, biological_age, depth, gwas, hla, imputationpanel, paper, variantdiscovery. Steps whose analysis maps onto one of those directories get code=2 (public repo, plausibly exact); all other steps get code=1 (public repo present and Code Availability claims broad coverage, but no directory maps and the step is only reconstructable from prose). Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted. Data axis: the study's own 10,239 WGS genomes are controlled-access and, per Data Availability, not yet deposited ('will be made available ... following publication'), so data=1 for every step that touches Korea10K individual-level data; steps whose only additional input is public 1KGP data still take the Korea10K min of 1.

steps.label: Read trimming with fastp v0.23.2: platform-specific adapter removal, polyG tail trimming, removal of reads with mean base quality below Q20
Alignment of trimmed reads to GRCh38 with BWA-MEM v0.7.17 with read-group information
Coordinate sorting and duplicate marking with Picard v2.27.5
Base quality score recalibration with GATK BaseRecalibrator and ApplyBQSR v4.6.1.0
Per-sample variant calling with GATK HaplotypeCaller v4.6.1.0 in GVCF mode, ploidy adjusted for sex chromosomes
Aggregation of 10,239 GVCFs with GATK GenomicsDBImport and joint genotyping with GATK v4.6.1.0; output standardised to VCF v4.2
Variant quality score recalibration (VQSR) applied separately to SNPs and indels using dbSNP v156, Mills & 1000G Gold Standard, HapMap and Omni resources

Sample- and variant-level QC to a 9,000-individual unrelated cohort: biallelic/VQSR-PASS retention (chrY exempt), conversion to PLINK2 format, missingness >10% and heterozygosity +/-3 SD exclusion (205 samples), mean ABHet outside +/-2 SD exclusion (221 samples), KING relatedness in PLINK v2.0.0-a.6.13LM with kinship > 0.125 (800 samples), and variant filters (ABHet outside 0.4-0.6, hom allele balance >10%, >10% zero-AD genotypes, ExcessHet > 60, call rate < 99%, HWE p threshold)
Annotation of the 61,223,704 retained biallelic variants with Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) v115

Variant-discovery saturation analysis: cumulative unique-variant curves over 9,000 unrelated individuals across 100 random sample-order permutations without replacement, saturation defined as the median saturation point
Autosomal phasing of 9,013 unrelated genomes with SHAPEIT5 v5.1.1 (commit 990ed0d) for Korean reference-panel construction
Imputation from the Korea10K reference panel with Minimac3 v2.0.1

Imputation-accuracy benchmarking of the Korea10K, Korea4K and Korea1K panels: squared Pearson correlation between imputed dosages and observed genotypes stratified by allele frequency, computed with the 'GetCorrelation' step of the TOPMed imputation evaluation pipeline (https://github.com/sgagliano/UKB_WES_vs_TOPMed_IMP), retaining the sign for negatively correlated variants

Harmonisation and merge of 9,013 Korean genomes with 2,541 kinship-filtered 1KGP high-coverage genomes: reciprocal SNP intersection with PLINK2 (--extract-intersect) and merge with PLINK v1.9.0-b.7.11 (--bmerge), yielding 15,501,578 unfiltered autosomal variants

Post-merge QC and LD pruning for population structure: MAF < 1%, HWE p threshold, missing genotype rate > 1% exclusion (4,315,937 variants retained), then --indep-pairwise 200kb 1 0.5 pruning (850,281 variants; 850,871 all-population and 876,547 EAS-restricted sets) and principal-component computation

Identity-by-state clustering with PLINK1 (--cluster --K 5) producing 500 clusters, removal of clusters with <= 2 samples (485 retained), PC1-PC5 centroid-nearest representative selection, and merge of the 485 representatives with 2,541 1KGP individuals to 517,041 LD-pruned variants
Model-based ancestry estimation with ADMIXTURE v1.3.0 for K = 1 to 17 on variants additionally pruned with --indep-pairwise 500kb 1 0.2, optimal K chosen by lowest ten-fold cross-validation error
Liftover of Y-chromosome variants from GRCh38 to GRCh37 with GATK LiftoverVcf v4.6.1.0 for 5,975 male participants
Y-haplogroup classification with yhaplo v2.1.14.dev7+gf8b300b against the ISOGG 2016 phylogeny; 104 of 5,975 males unclassified, 5,871 retained, 5,290 unrelated males used for haplogroup proportions

Pairwise p-distance computation with VCF2Dis v1.54 on the VCF of 5,871 haplogroup-classified males, with 100 bootstrap replicates each drawing a random 25% of SNPs and a Newick tree inferred per replicate
Y-chromosome consensus-tree reconstruction and visualisation from the 100 bootstrap Newick trees with IQ-TREE3 v3.0.1
Extraction of chrM reads from whole-genome BAMs with samtools v1.18 and conversion to paired-end FASTQ

Mitochondrial genome assembly with NOVOPlasty v4.3 for 10,239 samples (genome range 12,000-21,000 bp, k-mer 39, max memory 20 GB, insert size 300 bp, read length 151 bp, Illumina PE, reduce ambiguous Ns on, automatic insert-size estimation on); 73 assemblies excluded, 10,166 circularised genomes retained
Consensus mitochondrial genome generation for the 73 non-circularised samples by applying mitochondrial variants to the rCRS reference with bcftools v1.21 (consensus)
Completeness annotation of the 10,166 circularised assemblies with MitoZ v3.5: annotate --species_name 'Homo sapiens' --genetic_code 2 --clade 'Chordata'
Mitochondrial haplogroup assignment for 10,239 individuals with Haplogrep3 v3.2.1 against PhyloTree Build 17.2 (phylotree-rcrs@17.2)
Rotation of each mitochondrial sequence to the rCRS start point at the first 30 bp of the CO2 gene, allowing up to four mismatches, using rotate v1.0
Multiple sequence alignment of the 10,166 circularised mitochondrial genomes plus rCRS and RSRS with MAFFT v7.525 (--auto)

Mitochondrial maximum-likelihood phylogeny with IQ-TREE3 v3.0.1: ModelFinder (MFP) search, final analysis under TIM3+F+I+R6, 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap replicates (-B 1000), 1,000 SH-aLRT replicates (-alrt 1000), 32 threads (-T 32)

Divergence-time estimation in MEGA12 under the RelTime framework: maximum-likelihood model, GTR+G+I with four discrete gamma categories, partial deletion at 95% site coverage, four haplogroup A/B/C/D calibration constraints, IQ-TREE Newick input, 3 threads

HLA-region read extraction and re-alignment: samtools v1.13 selection of unmapped reads / reads with unmapped mates, reads on chr6:29,844,528-33,100,696, and reads on HLA/ALT contigs (following get-reads-alt-unmap.sh), FASTQ conversion, BWA-MEM v0.7.17 re-alignment with default parameters to the GRCh38 chromosome 6 primary assembly, sort/index and restriction to chr6:29.8-33.1 Mb

HLA genotyping with xHLA (https://github.com/humanlongevity/HLA) on 10,239 samples, alleles reported at classical two-digit resolution; 9,000 unrelated individuals (18,000 haplotypes) used for HLA-A allele proportions

Identification and regional aggregation of CG-context-associated variants (CGVs): CG context index built from flanking nucleotides of reference and alternate alleles in GRCh38, allelic-presence scoring across the population, Korean-popular CGVs defined at >= 80% individual presence, mapping to 10-kb windows, net CG gain/loss normalised by total GRCh38 CG count, windows with >= 10% net change retained

Cross-population CGV allele-frequency comparison: allele counts via PLINK2 without prior biallelic filtering, multiallelic decomposition and left-normalisation with bcftools v1.21, directional variant selection within >= 10% CG-altered windows, chi-squared tests between Korean and 1KGP European samples, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction
Genomic annotation of CG-alteration hotspot intervals with Annotatr using the hg38_cpgs, hg38_basicgenes and hg38_enhancers_fantom annotation sets
Gene Ontology and pathway enrichment of hotspot-proximal genes with the ShinyGO and GeDiPNet web servers, FDR-corrected, significance at FDR < 0.05
Sample collection and DNA extraction: peripheral blood or saliva, DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit (Qiagen) for blood and GeneAll Exgene Clinic SV Mini Kit for saliva, QC on Qubit 3.0 and Bioanalyzer 2100

Library preparation: enzymatic fragmentation of high-molecular-weight DNA, TruSeq Nano / TruSeq PCR-Free (Illumina) or MGIEasy FS DNA Library Prep (BGI) kits, circularisation and rolling-circle amplification for DNBSEQ-T7 libraries
Whole-genome sequencing at mean 30x depth on MGI DNBSEQ-T7 (N = 6,311), Illumina NovaSeq 6000 (N = 2,832) and HiSeq X Ten (N = 1,096), 2 x 150 bp (151 bp for Illumina) paired-end

headline.static_readiness: 0/36 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 28/36 (78%) RI at the stage-1 ceiling. This paper is unusually well pinned at the prose level: fastp v0.23.2, BWA-MEM v0.7.17, Picard v2.27.5, GATK v4.6.1.0, PLINK v2.0.0-a.6.13LM, PLINK v1.9.0-b.7.11, VEP v115, SHAPEIT5 v5.1.1 (commit 990ed0d), Minimac3 v2.0.1, ADMIXTURE v1.3.0, yhaplo v2.1.14.dev7+gf8b300b, VCF2Dis v1.54, IQ-TREE3 v3.0.1, samtools v1.18 and v1.13, NOVOPlasty v4.3, bcftools v1.21, MitoZ v3.5, Haplogrep3 v3.2.1 (phylotree-rcrs@17.2), rotate v1.0 and MAFFT v7.525 all carry exact version strings, and several steps state full command lines. The 8 NI steps fall short on a single axis: C9 (VEP, no parameters at all), C10 and C33 (custom analyses with no software named), C13 (third-party TOPMed evaluation repo cited with no commit or tag), C30 (MEGA12 major version only, GUI), C32 (xHLA cited by repo URL with no version or commit), C35 (Annotatr unversioned), C36 (ShinyGO and GeDiPNet web servers, no code artifact). Because the repository carries no lockfile, no container, no conda environment file and no release tag, environment closure is absent, so under the Delta-2 reading no step can exceed version = 1 and no step is R-star-eligible even with stage-2 code verification.
headline.coverage: 36 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus the GitHub landing-page and README prose; 3 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. A Data Availability statement is present but names no accession: the Korea10K raw data 'will be made available through the Korea BioData Station (K-BDS)' only 'following publication', under IRB and Data Access Committee approval. A Code Availability statement is present and names https://github.com/korean-genomics-center/Korea10K, which resolves and is public. Note that of the study's stated 'multiomic' scope, the Methods describe only the WGS-derived analyses; no methylation, transcriptome or proteome processing steps appear in the Methods text, so none are scored here.

gaps.where: Software environment for all 36 computational steps (repository root; Methods)
gaps.missing: No lockfile, container image, conda environment file, renv.lock, module list or requirements file anywhere in the repository or the paper. Direct checks returned HTTP 404 for environment.yml, Dockerfile, requirements.txt, renv.lock, conda.yaml, nextflow.config and Snakefile on the default branch. The README is 165 bytes long and contains only the project title and an 'In submission' note - no system requirements, no installation instructions, no version table. Twenty-one distinct tools carry exact prose pins, which is the strongest part of this paper's readiness, but exact pins without environment closure cap the version axis at 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a conda-lock / pixi.lock or a container image digest covering the full GATK-Picard-BWA-samtools-bcftools-PLINK-SHAPEIT5-Minimac3-IQ-TREE-MAFFT-NOVOPlasty-MitoZ stack, plus a resolved R/Python environment for the custom saturation, CGV and plotting code. Given how thoroughly the versions are already documented in prose, a single lock artifact would convert most of the 28 RI steps into stage-2 R-star candidates.

gaps.missing: The primary input - the 10,239 Korean whole genomes - has no accession number of any kind. The statement is 'Raw data of Korea10K will be made available through the Korea BioData Station (K-BDS), provided by the Korea Bioinformation Center (KOBIC), following publication. Prior to public release, access to the Korea10K data can be granted upon request under appropriate data use agreements.' There is no dataset identifier, no DAC contact, no application URL and no timeline, so at the preprint state no reader can obtain the input by any documented route. Only the comparison datasets (1KGP Phase 3 30x via AWS Open Data, 1KGP Phase 1 legacy via the EBI FTP release of 2013-05-02) are resolvable.
gaps.how_to_close: Register the K-BDS submission and cite its accession identifier plus the Data Access Committee application URL in the Data Availability statement, even while the data remain under controlled access. Additionally deposit the aggregate artifacts that carry no re-identification risk - the 61,223,704-variant allele-frequency table and the imputation reference panel - under an open accession.

gaps.missing: No release, no tag and no commit hash is cited. The releases page reports no published releases and the Code Availability statement points at the default branch only, so the code state a reader retrieves is not pinned to the state the paper describes. The paper's own claim of repository scope ('variant calling pipelines, quality control procedures, population genetic analysis scripts, and imputation panel construction workflows') is only partially matched by the visible top-level tree (admixture_and_pca, backup, biological_age, depth, gwas, hla, imputationpanel, paper, variantdiscovery); there is a directory named 'backup' at top level and none for mitochondrial, Y-chromosome or CGV analysis.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release archived to Zenodo (or cite the submission-time commit SHA) and reference that immutable identifier in the Code Availability statement; remove or document the 'backup' directory.

gaps.where: C18-C30 (Y-chromosome and mitochondrial analyses), C33-C36 (CGV identification, aggregation, annotation and enrichment), C13 (imputation benchmarking)
gaps.missing: Seventeen of the thirty-six computational steps map to no directory in the repository. The mitochondrial pipeline (samtools extraction, NOVOPlasty assembly, bcftools consensus, MitoZ annotation, Haplogrep3, rotate, MAFFT, IQ-TREE3, MEGA12), the Y-chromosome pipeline (LiftoverVcf, yhaplo, VCF2Dis bootstrapping, IQ-TREE3 consensus) and the entire CGV analysis - which is the paper's principal novel methodological contribution - have no executable artifact named anywhere. The CG context index construction, the >= 80% population-prevalence rule and the 10-kb window normalisation are described in prose only.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the mitochondrial, Y-chromosome and CGV analysis code, including the CG-context indexing implementation and the window aggregation script, so the novel CGV result is executable rather than only described.

gaps.where: C9 (VEP), C5-C7 (GATK calling and VQSR), C10 (saturation permutations), C13 (imputation benchmark), C16/C17/C20/C29 (stochastic steps), C34 (statistical tests)
gaps.missing: VEP v115 is named with no options, no cache/assembly specification and no plugin list. GATK HaplotypeCaller ploidy handling is described only as 'adjusting ploidy for sex chromosomes' with no interval or ploidy map; VQSR tranche levels, annotation sets and the release versions of the Mills, HapMap and Omni resource bundles are unstated (only dbSNP v156 is pinned). No random seed is given for any stochastic step: the 100 saturation permutations, PLINK --cluster, ADMIXTURE, the 100 VCF2Dis bootstrap replicates drawing 25% of SNPs, or IQ-TREE3 ultrafast bootstrap. The imputation benchmark test set is defined only by reference to a prior study (Jeon et al., 2020). The software implementing the chi-squared tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction in C34 is not named.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the command lines and resource-bundle releases for the GATK and VEP steps, record random seeds for all stochastic analyses, state the imputation benchmark sample list explicitly, and name the statistical implementation used for the CGV comparison.

gaps.missing: Four analyses depend on tools whose backing databases change over time with no recorded release: ShinyGO and GeDiPNet are web servers invoked with no version and no access date, and their GO/pathway database releases determine the enrichment result; xHLA is cited by repository URL only, so its bundled HLA allele database release is unrecorded; Annotatr's hg38_cpgs / hg38_basicgenes / hg38_enhancers_fantom annotation sets are Bioconductor packages whose releases are unstated; MEGA12 is a GUI tool cited by major version only.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the server version and access date for each web-tool invocation and the release of every annotation database, or replace the web invocations with locally installed, version-pinned equivalents.

gaps.where: C8 (Sample and Variant Filtering), C15 (post-merge QC)
gaps.missing: The Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium p-value thresholds are unreadable in the published text: the filtering section states 'Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE) p-value < 1x10OO' and the population-structure section states 'HWE with P < 10OO', where the exponent has been lost in typesetting. A reader cannot reproduce either QC step without guessing the exponent, and the two thresholds may differ.
gaps.how_to_close: Correct the typeset exponents in both Methods passages, and state the HWE test variant (midp / keep-fewhet) and the PLINK flag used.

gaps.where: Study scope vs Methods coverage (title, abstract, Methods)
gaps.missing: The paper is titled and framed as a 'multiomic' reference dataset, and the repository contains a 'biological_age' and a 'gwas' directory, but the Methods describe no multiomic data processing at all - there is no methylation, transcriptome, proteome or metabolome analysis section, and no clinical-phenotype processing section. Results referencing multiomic biomarkers cite prior publications rather than methods in this paper. The multiomic and clinical layers are therefore not assessable for computational readiness from this text.
gaps.how_to_close: Add Methods sections describing the generation and processing of the multiomic and clinical layers, or scope the title and abstract to the whole-genome component that the Methods actually cover.

gaps.where: W1-W3: sample collection and DNA extraction, library preparation, whole-genome sequencing on three platforms
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted. Note that the three-platform design (MGI DNBSEQ-T7 61.6%, NovaSeq 6000 27.7%, HiSeq X Ten 10.7%) is a documented batch-effect source that no computational step in the Methods explicitly corrects for.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the analysis from raw reads onward. A platform-covariate sensitivity analysis would nonetheless strengthen the downstream population-genetic claims.
